THE GATE LIFECYCLE, DERIVED ONCE (12/08) — delivered at 1dc9b92.

WHAT LANDED. ONE pure module over the event tail, src/store/workflow.ts:
`gateLifecycle(events, gate) -> none|submitted|accepted|rejected` (the LAST of the
submitted|confirmed|rejected triple — the ONLY interpreter of that triple in the
codebase now), `gateView` (the same one pass, carrying the accepted/submitted/rejected
indices, the last decision, the last rejection and the undecided wait that its readers
ask for), and ONE `workflowState(events)`: the status WORD + the DERIVED `rework` flag
(a rejected bound gate with no later submission at it; a re-submission clears it) +
waitingOn/pendingWait + the derived `next` verdict. The ~11 independent re-readings are
gone: Store.taskStatus/detail/gateProblems/check, Commands.gateState /
undecidedSubmission / pendingGates / rejections, lookBack (sharing ONE pendingGatesOf
scan with the whole-journey queue), the Frame's PRIVATE gateState (DELETED — with
pendingWait = undischargedWait and latestRejection = the view's), the transcript's
attempt boundary / verify-cycle anchor, the operator action's landing label, the eval
harness, and the UI's next-line branch table (which became a verdict→WORDING map: the
payload carries detail.next + detail.rework, the page only words them). The gate state
word is ONE vocabulary everywhere: `accepted` is what the event `confirmed` records.

THE RECONCILIATION RULE (AC-3). check() now fails when the status word contradicts the
derived lifecycle: GATE-REWORK for a READY word (queued/active) beside a last-decision
rejection at a bound gate, GATE-STATUS for `accepted` without a confirm accept, and
GATE-STATUS for `blocked` with neither an undecided submission nor an undischarged
`waiting`. The proof is a pre-existing fixture asserting the bug: the what's-next e2e's
"no submission" journey carried a task whose grill gate was REJECTED and asserted
`integrity.clean === true`, `executable === true`, continue-leg (its comment read "one
task whose grill gate was REJECTED (a DECIDED gate, so the integrity check is clean)").
It now reports the NAMED GATE-REWORK blocker over HTTP and POST /api/approve refuses
`refused-integrity` with zero writes; the care-(a) daemon-prompt case moved to the
un-submitted state it is about. LIVE JOURNEY: `ann check` is CLEAN — no live task
carries a READY word beside a last-decision rejection (12/05's rework was cleared by its
re-submission at grill; 11/01 and 12/02 re-submitted before confirming), so the rule
flags nothing live and no history was touched. `ann verify` clean; the finding travels
through check() into advance!'s integrity re-check, the WHAT'S NEXT card and
GET /api/integrity, so the steering surface can no longer call a contradiction clean.

RESIDUAL, NAMED (12/06's scope, not this task's): frontmostReady still offers a
rework-owed task and advance() still says `continue-leg` — the guard is the integrity
refusal, not the proposal. That is the deliberate division: this task makes the
contradiction FAIL (AC-3), 12/06 makes it READ (the `rework` line at the steering
surface).

COORDINATION — HOW 12/06 (`06-implementation-rework-visible`) MUST NOW CONSUME THIS
(its AC-1/AC-2/AC-4, and the reason it must not re-implement the word):
  · the flag: `workflowState(events).rework` (or `Store.detail(id).rework`, already in
    the /api/confirm payload) — a task is rework-owed iff that is true; do NOT re-derive
    "last decision is a rejection" anywhere.
  · the target + the reason: `workflowState(events).gates[gate]` gives `gate`,
    `state === 'rejected'`, and `lastRejection.feedback` (the human's own words — the
    SAME reading the frame's rework prompt uses), so the next/look-back line can say
    REWORK + the gate + the feedback.
  · the card's line: the verdict `{verdict: 'rework', gate}` is ALREADY derived
    (`detail.next`) and worded by the page — 12/06 should extend the wording/marker
    rather than add a second derivation.
  · the question 12/06 must settle (recorded in my report for the operator/human): its
    AC-1 allows a `rework` STATUS WORD; adding one to `vocab.statuses` + the projection
    would make the status word itself honest — but it would also make this task's
    AC-3(a) reconciliation rule unreachable (a contradiction that can no longer occur
    cannot be reported). Either order works; if 12/06 adds the word, it must retire
    (a) and say so explicitly, because the rule and the word are the same fact seen from
    two sides. My recommendation: keep the status word READY and the rework explicit
    (flag + verdict + line), which is what this task built and what the reconciliation
    consumes.

claims.statement: ONE derivation over the event tail + ONE workflow-state projection, and it is the ONLY interpreter of the submitted|confirmed|rejected triple: src/store/workflow.ts exports gateLifecycle(events, gate) -> none|submitted|accepted|rejected (the LAST of the triple), gateView (the same ONE pass, with the facts its readers need: the accepted/submitted/rejected indices, the last decision, the last rejection, the undecided wait) and workflowState(events) = the status word + the DERIVED rework flag + waitingOn/pendingWait + the derived next verdict. The lifecycle is unit-tested across the WHOLE range: created-only (none) . first submission (submitted) . accept (accepted) . reject (rejected + rework) . RE-submission after a reject (the rework CLEARED) . accept after rework . a decision at the OTHER gate leaving this one untouched . a double decision at one gate (the LAST wins, both directions) . an empty tail . a legacy/inert tail (unknown type, gateless submission, status-inert goal-met, bookkeeping extended) . and a long tail where the view's indices/counts/last-rejection are pinned exactly.

EVERY reader consumes the derivation and the duplicates are gone. The store: taskStatus = workflowState(evs).status; detail().gates/rework/next/blockers from the gate views; gateProblems' GATE-1/GATE-2/GATE-SEQ read the views' accepted/submitted indices. The command layer: gateState = gateView().state, undecidedSubmission = gateView().undecided, rejections = gateView().rejected.length, and pendingGates + lookBack share ONE pendingGatesOf scan (the whole-journey queue and the active-leg observer view can no longer be two readings). L2: the Frame's PRIVATE gateState is DELETED (gateLifecycle), pendingWait = undischargedWait, latestRejection = the view's lastRejection; Transcript.boundary = lastRejection.index, verifyCycles = lastDecisionIndex, runId = rejected.length; operator-action's landing label = the projection's waitingOn; the eval harness reads the views. The UI payload: detail.next (the DERIVED verdict) + detail.rework ride /api/confirm, and ui.ts only WORDS the verdict (nextLine is a verdict->wording map; the one local input is the gate IN HAND). A reader-AGREEMENT table pins all FOUR states across 11 readers (status . detail gates . rework . next . gateState . undecidedSubmission . blockers . rejections . pendingGates . lookBack . the reconciliation), plus a source guard that no file outside workflow.ts scans the triple.

The reconciliation rule is SCRIPTED in check() (workflowProblems): GATE-REWORK when a READY status word (queued/active) stands beside a last-decision REJECTION at a bound gate (the mis-dispatch), GATE-STATUS when `accepted` has no confirm accept, GATE-STATUS when `blocked` has neither an undecided submission nor an undischarged `waiting`. advance!'s integrity re-check, the whatsnext card and GET /api/integrity all read check(), so the steering surface can no longer call a contradiction clean - PROVEN against a fixture that asserted exactly that: src/e2e/whats-next.e2e.test.ts's pre-existing 'no submission' fixture carried a task whose grill gate was REJECTED and asserted integrity.clean === true, executable === true and continue-leg (its own comment: 'one task whose grill gate was REJECTED (a DECIDED gate, so the integrity check is clean)'); it now reports the NAMED GATE-REWORK blocker over HTTP and POST /api/approve refuses `refused-integrity` with ZERO writes, while the care-(a) daemon-prompt case moved to the genuinely un-submitted state it is about. The unit fixture pins the same shape: the pre-existing rules (gateProblems, every other check rule) report NOTHING and only the new finding is present. LIVE JOURNEY: ann check is CLEAN - no live task carries a READY word beside a last-decision rejection (12/05's rework was cleared by its re-submission at grill; 11/01 and 12/02 re-submitted before confirming), so the rule flags no live state and no history was touched.

The projection invents no state: `rework` is DERIVED (a bound gate whose LAST decision is a rejection with no later submission at it; a re-submission clears it) - no new event type, no new stored field, no new write path (the diff adds no writer and no event). The reject bound (3/gate) stays gate!'s constant, the rework rung and the F-AC16 closure semantics are untouched. THE CONTRAST IS PINNED: a freshly-ACCEPTED entry gate still derives queued/ready (next: entry-accepted) and a reject-after-three-cycles still derives the same WORD with rework=true - the word alone cannot tell them apart, which is exactly why the flag and the reconciliation exist. The terminals are pinned unchanged: done . failed . cancelled . deferred never yield to a wait, superseded is unchanged, the two-phase wait (confirm accepted + undischarged `waiting`) still blocks and the commit evidence still releases it into the honest `accepted`, and goal-met stays status-inert.

The two decision vocabularies are REGISTERED as a reconciliation: rules/schema/vocab.json (v4) declares gateDecisions {accept: confirmed, reject: rejected}, its code literal is GATE_DECISION_EVENTS in the ONE derivation (what gate! now writes and gateLifecycle reads), and the knowing duplicate is recorded in the reconciliation register (docs/resource-registry.md section 5, plus the section 3 schema row and the AGENTS.md docs index). A TABLE test pins it: the registry equals the code literal; the mapping is TOTAL and injective (keys exactly accept|reject, values in the triple, no third form); the CLOSED gate set is grill|confirm; and per gate event type the ALLOWED FIELDS are exercised through the REAL single writer (each allowed field accepted, an unknown field refused BY NAME, a gate outside the closed set refused) - so a silent third form or a widened field set fails the suite.

No regression, committed with evidence at 1dc9b92: full npm test 46 files / 840 tests green (baseline 45/793 - +45 workflow unit tests and +2 whats-next e2e; the only pre-existing assertions touched are the ones that asserted the OLD gate-state word `confirmed` for the card's gate (now `accepted`, one vocabulary) and the fixture that asserted the rejected-gate state was integrity-clean). npm run typecheck clean, npm run build clean, ann check OK (13 docs in the manifest, no gate gaps), ann verify clean (0 drifts) - all five captured at 1dc9b92. The leg status / leg gate / goal exhaustion / the closed set are untouched: CLOSED_TASK_STATUSES is unchanged and the status derivation preserves every previous case's order semantics (an accept sets the accepted word exactly where its event sits in the tail).

feedback:
Review verdict — no 🔴 regression, and the sharpest risk is cleared

 The 22× validator speed-up changes no rule's outcome — verified two independent ways (the diff's resolution semantics, and a per-sha-vs-batch
 probe over the live journey with zero disagreements). The write guard and the reject bound are untouched. Both landings implement their ACs
 (not just claim them); the fresh evidence reproduces (840/46, check/verify clean).

 But it found two correctness-adjacent defects worth your attention before you accept 12/08

 F1 (substantive) — reconciliation condition (b) (accepted without a confirm accept) is reachable through the sanctioned writers, its message
 names a condition that is false in that case, and the comment asserting it "unreachable" is wrong. → dev-task fix (behaviour-preserving, two
 words) + a test for the accept→re-submit→reject shape.

 F2 (design, and it's the big one) — as implemented, the projection derives status='queued' + rework=true for a rejected gate, and rule (a)
 declares exactly that output illegal → so the module both derives the state and forbids it, and the only guard against the mis-dispatch is a
 journey-wide check() failure — meaning: from the moment a human rejects one gate, every read fails integrity and advance! refuses until the
 rework is resubmitted. A normal act with an outsized blast radius.

 F3 / G1 — two spellings of the same read (a private wrapper beside the direct call); a false comment in approve.ts.

 F5–F11, G2–G5 — 🟡 quality only (one cleanup pass). G6 — not reproducible; mechanism verified instead.

 The 12/06 tension — now sharp, with a recommendation

 The reviewer's position (opposite to the implementer's):

 │ Take the status word rework; retire rule (a). Prevention beats detection: a task not in the ready set cannot be proposed — versus making
 │ the whole journey fail check() at every read. Keep the rework flag + the next verdict either way (they carry the gate + the feedback a bare
 │ word can't); keep the word out of CLOSED_TASK_STATUSES and the leg/distance reads.

 So on 12/06's entry gate you're really deciding: word (prevention) vs flag + rule (detection) — and whichever you pick, 12/08 needs the
 matching fix (F1, plus F2 if you keep the flag-and-rule).
